note: Theseus carries off the child Helen and hides her at Aphidnae — the bride the Dioscuri reclaim and Paris will one day take to Troy.
Come down for Cerberus on his last labour, Heracles finds the bound comrades and raises Theseus from the Chair of Forgetfulness.
The same death told in two arms: Deianira's shirt steeped in Nessus' blood consumes Heracles on the pyre.
At Knossos the labyrinth Daedalus built for Minos holds the Minotaur Theseus comes to slay.
Theseus flees Crete with Ariadne and puts in at Dia — where Dionysus takes her and the black sail sends Aegeus to his death.
Medea of Colchis, fled from Jason, reaches Aegeus' Athens and all but poisons the arriving Theseus.
Seeking news of his father, Telemachus comes to sandy Pylos to the old charioteer Nestor — the one captain who reached home unharmed.
From Pylos Telemachus rides to Sparta, where Menelaus tells of Proteus and the long road back from Egypt.
Orpheus' counter-melody lets the Argo pass the Sirens when Butes alone swims to their isle.
Like Theseus and Pirithous, Orpheus descends alive to Hades — but charms the rulers of the dead with song rather than force.
Actaeon son of Aristaeus and Autonoe, bred by Chiron to the chase, is torn by his own hounds on Cithaeron — the grief that drives his father from Greece.
Long-haired Aristaeus weds Autonoe in the Cadmean house — binding the bee-keeper's craft to the royal line of Cadmus and Harmonia.
Apollodorus cites Acusilaus: Zeus destroyed Actaeon because he wooed Semele — one of three rival charges against Cadmus' hunter-grandson.
